[[Category:Transformer]]
'''Self-attention''' is the process through which a [[Transformer]] enriches its [[token embedding (machine learning)|token embedding vectors]] with contextual information derived from other tokens in the same token sequence.<ref>{{#cite:Q3130}}</ref>

== Definition ==

Let $\mathbf{X}\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times d}$ be the '''vector embedding matrix''' of [[token (machine learning)|token sequence]] $X$, in which row $t$ is the embedding vector for the token at position $t$.

$$
\mathbf{Q}=\mathbf{X}\mathbf{W}_Q,
\qquad
\mathbf{K}=\mathbf{X}\mathbf{W}_K,
\qquad
\mathbf{V}=\mathbf{X}\mathbf{W}_V.
$$

where $\mathbf{W}_Q,\mathbf{W}_K,\mathbf{W}_V\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d_k}$ are '''weight matrices''' learnt during training (e.g., via [[backpropagation]]).

Then the stadard attention score
$$
S_\text{attention}=\operatorname{Attention}(\mathbf{Q},\mathbf{K},\mathbf{V})
=
\operatorname{row-wise softmax}\left(\frac{\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^{\top}}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)\mathbf{V},
$$

<blockquote>
The [[Softmax|softmax]] is taken row-wise so for each embedding vector $\vec x_t$ within $X$, $\sum_{i=1}^{d_k} (S_{\text{attention})_{t,i} =1$.

The scaling factor $1/\sqrt{d_k}$ keeps the scores from growing with the dimension.

Both are [[normalisation function]]s applied for numerical stability.
</blockquote>

<ref>{{#cite:Q3130}}</ref>
== Complexity ==

The score matrix $\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^{\top}$ is $T\times T$, so attention over a context of length $T$ costs $\mathcal{O}(T^2 d)$ time and $\mathcal{O}(T^2)$ memory. Generating a sequence recomputes most of this work unless the keys and values computed and cached, such as via [[KV caching]].

<ref>{{#cite:Q3130}}</ref>
